title: A Framework for Characterizing Hair-Image Texture Across Spatial Scales: Application to Japanese Women’s Hair
content: Hair appearance reflects the organization of fibers and bundles across spatial scales, but quantitative descriptions of this organization remain limited. We examined the scale dependence of transverse hair-image texture using detrending moving average (DMA) analysis of back-view photographs of 145 Japanese women. We used synthetic images to assess the effects of signal length, orientation, and spatial heterogeneity and to guide the choice of analysis conditions. Across many participants and hair regions, fluctuation functions exhibited approximate power-law scaling over the finite range analyzed. Most DMA exponents were within 0.5 < \( \alpha_{\mathrm{est}} \) <1.0, and larger exponents were associated with visually coarser textures. Among 86 participants whose hair tips were visible, exponent profiles differed substantially between individuals, while the population mean showed systematic variation from the crown toward the hair tips. DMA(0) and DMA(2) yielded broadly similar results, with local discrepancies in regions with strong spatial variation in image intensity. These findings identify a statistical relationship between fine- and coarse-scale intensity fluctuations, providing a basis for investigating hair appearance across scales. Future studies linking scaling properties to physical measurements and visual assessments could support evaluation of changes induced by products and hairdressing techniques.
